entries.title: Logan v Logan, and the Crown Slips Off Geo's Head Overnight
entries.subtitle: Joe quietly hoovers up seven points in a Group F he practically owns outright, while Sean wins a game that helps precisely nobody
entries.html:
Of all the bulletins to crackle out of a Thursday — earthquakes, courtrooms, the eternal forensic accounting of royal money — the dispatch that detained this desk was the news that Canada has been ruled eligible for Eurovision. Picture it: the Maple Leaf, sequinned, lunging for a key change somewhere over the Atlantic. Spare a thought, then, for Barney, whose Canada is presently the only act in his repertoire still holding a tune, because while his maple darlings rehearse their power ballad the rest of his roster spent the night being booed clean off the stage.

Group E — Logan declares war on himself

First, the funeral. 🇨🇼 Curaçao went down 0-2 to 🇨🇮 Ivory Coast, Joe's Ivorians strolling into second and the knockouts while Barney's islanders — one goal scored, nine conceded across the whole sorry run — bow out looking like men who turned up to the wrong continent. Then came the night's great act of self-cannibalism: 🇪🇨 Ecuador 2-1 🇩🇪 Germany, a fixture in which Logan owned both dugouts. There is something gloriously KluivertEye about it — a man running his own false-flag operation, leaking the result to himself in advance. Germany top the group regardless, so Logan loses nothing and bags the Ecuador win on top; his plucky underdogs now sit third, fingernails bitten to the quick in the best-third lottery.

Group F — the Strait of HorMousaDembele runs it all

If anyone owns a postcode here it is Joe, landlord of three of the four sides. 🇹🇳 Tunisia 1-3 🇳🇱 Netherlands was Joe playing Joe, his Dutch flagship cantering to the group summit on seven while his Tunisians slunk off played three, lost three, nil — the worst kind of in-house result, profit and loss in the same ledger. Alongside it, 🇯🇵 Japan 1-1 🇸🇪 Sweden split Logan and Joe down the middle: Logan's Japan qualify second, Joe's Swedes left third and sweating. All told Joe banked a tournament-best seven points without breaking sweat — the trade routes, for once, gloriously open.

Group D — a win for nothing, a point for an empire

Sean's 🇹🇷 Turkey beat Pete's 🇺🇸 United States 3-2 in the most pointless triumph of the campaign — Turkey eliminated anyway, the USA topping the group anyway. Three sweepstake points for Sean, zero for Pete, whose Americans waltzed through while their owner got nothing for it; pure Nico Ol'Gilly hard luck, winning the lottery and finding the ticket's gone through the wash. And in 🇵🇾 Paraguay 0-0 🇦🇺 Australia, Geo's Socceroos ground out second place on a single, grey, ThomasTwoShell point — the scowl of a man delivering a tactical lecture to a room that has quietly left. Barney's Paraguay cling to third and the lottery.

The reckoning

Yesterday this column signed off on Geo the emperor with the words “long may he reign — until tomorrow, when football comes for everybody.” Football, punctual as ever, came for him inside twenty-four hours. Logan's +4 vaulted him from second to top of the £60 player league on 36, nudging Geo — marooned on a single point — off the throne he'd held for one night flat; level on points, but the order has flipped. Joe's +7 was the haul of the evening and yanked him level with Barney on 27, while also wresting League 4 away from Barney's Canada and handing it to Ivory Coast. Sean ticked up three for his beautiful, useless win. And Pete? Pete moved not a muscle — still rooted to the foot on 16, the man who owns a group winner and somehow leaves with empty hands. On the night: Joe and Logan. In the tables: a new name on top, and Geo glaring at the standings like a deposed king who can't quite believe the coup took an afternoon.

entries.title: Geo Conquers, Qatar Crumbles, and Pete Plumbs the Haitian Depths
entries.subtitle: A night the Thomas TwoShell empire ate itself in Group A — and still came out smelling of roses
entries.html:
Lo, on the Night of Wednesday 24 June the heavens opened and rained nine sweepstake points upon the chosen, while the wretched were left to gnash their teeth in the away end — and nobody, but nobody, gnashed harder than Pete.

Group B — Switzerland take it, Geo eats himself again

🇨🇭 Switzerland did exactly what Switzerland do, settling 🇨🇦 Canada 2-1 with the cold efficiency of a numbered bank account, topping the group on seven and handing Geo a tidy haul. Spare a thought, then, for Barney, whose Canada still squeak through in second yet contributed the grand sum of sod all to his evening. Meanwhile 🇧🇦 Bosnia-Herzegovina battered 🇶🇦 Qatar 3-1 — Logan's underdogs feasting on Geo's other lamb. Qatar, with two goals for and TEN against, depart the tournament looking like they wandered into the wrong stadium and apologised the whole way through.

Group C — Brazil purr, Scotland perish, Pete's Haitian horror

🏴󠁧󠁢󠁳󠁣󠁴󠁿 Scotland were taken behind the bike sheds by 🇧🇷 Brazil, 0-3, and Sean's Tartan Army now sit third, biting their nails through the best-third lottery like a man waiting on a hospital scan. Brazil cruise. And in the night's true bloodbath, 🇲🇦 Morocco put four past 🇭🇹 Haiti, Logan banking yet more while Pete's Haiti slunk off with played three, lost three, nil points — a campaign of such unrelenting calamity it deserves its own Netflix documentary and a grief counsellor.

Group A — the house of Thomas TwoShell devours its own

Here, dear watcher, was farce of the highest order. 🇲🇽 Mexico dismantled Logan's 🇨🇿 Czechia 0-3 to finish a flawless nine points, knocking Germany off the summit of League 1 in the process. Then came the fixture for the philosophers: 🇿🇦 South Africa 1-0 🇰🇷 South Korea — Geo versus Geo, a man arm-wrestling himself in the mirror and somehow losing one hand. South Africa qualify second, South Korea wobble into third, and Geo simply shrugged, having owned every single boot on the pitch.

The Reckoning

And so to the ledger. Geo banked NINE points, vaulting from second to top of the £60 player league on 35, and now leads Leagues 1, 2 and 3 through Mexico and Switzerland — an emperor surveying his realm even as Qatar and South Korea bleed out at his feet. Logan matched him point for point, also +9, climbing third to second on 32 and crowning Bosnia atop League 7. The cruellest twist belongs to Barney, who walked in leading the whole thing and walked out third, undone not by his own teams but by the sheer relentlessness of the two men above him. Joe (a stationary fourth) and Sean (fifth) merely watched. And Pete? Pete props up the table on 16, the proud owner of the only side on the planet to lose all three, a man whose World Cup is now purely spectatorial. On the night: Geo and Logan feasted. In the tables: Geo is king. Long may he reign — until tomorrow, when football, as ever, comes for everybody.
